messages:
morgan: Hey — running into a few issues with redwoodctl on my M1 mac. Brew install fails in post_install. Copy of the output below. Anyone seen this?

morgan: ```
Error: failed during post_install
mkdir: /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl: permission denied
```

morgan: Also, after I got a binary via the curl installer, `redwoodctl profile use staging` didn’t actually switch — `redwoodctl whoami` still showed prod.

jamal: Which macOS / Homebrew versions? Did you try `brew update` + `brew uninstall redwoodctl` then reinstall? Could be permissions on /opt/homebrew.

morgan: macOS 13.6.1, Homebrew 4.0.0. Tried uninstall/reinstall, same error. Workaround: curl installer produced a binary that runs, but `redwoodctl auth login` opens my browser and the redirect back errors with a 502 while I'm on corp VPN.

sophia: Corp VPN + SSO often breaks the browser redirect flow. We have a device flow: `redwoodctl auth login --device` (older CLIs used `--browserless`). That prints a code and URL you paste into a browser on a machine with access.

morgan: Tried `--device` — login succeeded. But `redwoodctl profile use staging` still appears to read prod from `~/.redwood/config.json` (I also have `~/.redwood/config.yaml` and `~/.redwood/token.json`). Which file is authoritative?

olivia: `config.yaml` (or `config.json` depending on OS) is the source of truth for profiles. `token.json` stores tokens keyed by profile. There was a regression in 0.9.1 where `profile use` updated in-memory state but didn’t persist to config on disk, so whoami could still show the old tenant.

morgan: Ah — I’m on 0.9.1. Upgrading might help. Also noticed CLI ignores `REDWOOD_API_URL` I set for local private deployment testing — it still hit hosted endpoints after switching profiles.

jamal: CLI precedence should be: CLI flags > env `REDWOOD_API_URL` > profile.endpoint in config. If you installed an older binary from the curl installer, it may not implement the env precedence fix. `redwoodctl version` to confirm.

morgan: `redwoodctl version` shows v0.9.1. Upgraded to v0.9.3 and reran tests. `REDWOOD_API_URL` override now respected and `profile use` persists. Good catch.

morgan: Quick summary / UX feedback to file: 
- Homebrew installer doesn't detect M1 Homebrew path (`/opt/homebrew`) correctly and tries to mkdir with sudo; should detect and avoid permission errors.
- Device auth flag names inconsistent between releases (`--device` vs `--browserless`) — pick one and keep it.
- When running with `--debug` print the exact config file path and token file being used so users aren’t guessing between `config.yaml`, `config.json`, and `token.json`.

sophia: +1 on debug output and a clear table of precedence in the docs. We should also document token cache TTL and `redwoodctl auth refresh` behavior — people hit stale tokens a lot.

devex-bot: Quick reference: device auth docs -> https://docs.redwood.ai/cli/auth#device-flow :link:

olivia: @morgan can you open a tiny bug with steps to reproduce the Homebrew post_install failure and attach `brew gist-logs redwoodctl`? We'll triage and see if installer script needs path detection changes.

morgan: Will do and attach logs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
